children: Markets opened lower on Tuesday, September 29, with the Nifty 50 falling to 22,673.85, down 106.40 points or 0.47 per cent from its previous close of 22,780.25, while the Sensex slipped to 72,385.06, shedding 386.66 points or 0.53 per cent from its previous close of 72,771.72. Both indices opened weak, the Nifty at 22,732.45 and the Sensex at 72,633.68, extending Monday's sharp selloff where the Nifty had lost 360 points and the Sensex 1,124 points.

The sell-off comes as Brent crude trades above $106 a barrel and the US 10-year Treasury yield hovers at 5.23–5.24 per cent, its highest since 2007. Dr. V K Vijayakumar, Chief Investment Strategist at Geojit Investments, said the global macro construct "continues to be unfavourable for equity markets," warning that elevated US growth and inflation could warrant "one more rate hike by the Fed." He added that if crude prices remain elevated, "the fiscal strain can impact India's GDP growth and corporate earnings growth for FY27."

Monday's session saw broad-based selling with PSU Banks emerging as the biggest laggards, their sectoral index falling 3.15 per cent. Bank Nifty closed at 54,471.65, down 1,108.75 points or 1.99 per cent, after breaking below the key 55,000 level. India VIX surged 12.15 per cent to 13.6375, signalling elevated near-term volatility.

Foreign institutional investors remained net sellers for a third consecutive session, offloading equities worth over ₹5,353 crore on Monday, while domestic institutional investors provided some cushion with net purchases of around ₹5,189 crore. Hitesh Tailor, Technical Research Analyst at Choice Broking, noted that "persistent FII outflows continue to weigh on sentiment, although strong DII buying may provide some cushioning."

Among Tuesday's early gainers on the Nifty 50, pharma stocks led the pack. Dr. Reddy's Laboratories rose 1.98 per cent to ₹1,245.20, opening at ₹1,243.20. Cipla gained 1.02 per cent to ₹1,397.80, while Sun Pharmaceutical advanced 0.76 per cent to ₹1,851.90. In the auto sector, Eicher Motors edged up 0.37 per cent to ₹7,240.00. Coal India posted a modest gain of 0.19 per cent, trading at ₹423.30.

On the losing side, Tata Motors (TMPV) was the steepest decliner, falling 2.27 per cent to ₹275.35 from its previous close of ₹281.75. HDFC Life Insurance dropped 1.99 per cent to ₹521.00, while Bajaj Finance fell 1.43 per cent to ₹970.90 from a previous close of ₹985.00. Retail conglomerate Trent declined 1.29 per cent to ₹2,592.00, and HDFC Bank shed 1.24 per cent to ₹710.10, with the stock seeing the heaviest trading value at ₹29,034.84 lakhs.

title: Nifty slips below 22,700 as crude, US yields pile pressure on markets
